frequency_question: How often do highly contested, high-friction major voting/election integrity bills pass the U.S. Senate within a single Congress/two-year window?
membership_rule: Includes major federal voting, election administration, or franchise bills that lacked broad bipartisan consensus and faced cloture hurdles in the U.S. Senate from the 111th Congress (2009) through the 118th Congress (2024). Excludes routine omnibus appropriations or bills passing via budget reconciliation.

coverage_note: 6 distinct major legislative vehicles/pushes identified; represents the universe of high-friction partisan voting reforms tested against the Senate filibuster in this era.
known_gaps: Does not include committee-only stalled bills that never reached a floor cloture vote, though those would only reinforce the zero success rate.
skeleton: Total major highly-contested partisan federal voting/election bills introduced and brought to a cloture test in the Senate vs. those that successfully cleared the 60-vote threshold.
multiplier: 0 successes out of 6 distinct major legislative pushes since 2009 equals 0/6.
validity_reason: Valid through the end of the current structural rules era; remains stable as long as the 60-vote Senate filibuster rule for general legislation remains in place.
